title: QRÖMELIFE
excerpt: Quavo has released *QRÖMELIFE*, a 14-track solo album executive produced by Pharrell Williams and the follow-up to 2023's *Rocket Power*.
body:
Quavo has released *QRÖMELIFE*, a 14-track solo album executive produced by Pharrell Williams and the follow-up to 2023's *Rocket Power*. Takeoff's death is still part of the record, but grief no longer dictates every turn. Much of the album is about the ordinary life that continues around it.

The title comes from Quavo's idea of a "qrome" state, a word he connects to "chromosome." He uses it for the point when something painful becomes part of a person's makeup rather than an event that can simply be left behind. In his explanation, people still have to wake up, work and move through daily life while carrying what happened with them.

Pharrell worked on the album for more than a year and a half, with sessions at Louis Vuitton's headquarters in Paris and on a yacht in Miami. Quavo has said the collaboration pushed him back toward the versatility that once let him move between Migos records, solo hits and features. Across *QRÖMELIFE*, that range matters more than any single guest or production trick.

[apple:album:6817200688]

"Away" reunites Quavo and Offset on the album after the two repaired a relationship that had fractured publicly before Takeoff's death. The song follows their return to working together, while conversations about Migos have also resumed. Quavo has said any future group release would have to respect Takeoff's place in Migos rather than simply continue under the name without him.

He also recently became a father to a daughter. Quavo's own father died when he was four, and he has spoken about wanting to give his child the presence he did not have growing up. A short film released with *QRÖMELIFE* moves through older Migos footage, studio work and family history before closing on a shot of him holding his daughter.

The album arrived during an unexpected second life for "HOTEL LOBBY (Unc & Phew)," Quavo and Takeoff's 2022 single. Clips of the pair performing it have been pulled into a wave of AI-generated videos, something Quavo has admitted can be difficult to watch. He said the resurgence feels bigger than an internet trend because it keeps Takeoff present for people who still care about the music. Even with his discomfort around the technology, he is grateful that his nephew's name is still being spoken.
